# Commands reference

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask gen-docs`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every operation is a JSON object whose `type` is the operation name, followed by its parameters, e.g.

```json
{"type": "panel.create_rect", "width": 500, "height": 700}
```

IDs are strings such as `"panel:2"`. Lengths are in millimetres.
Errors are structured: a stable `code`, named `args` and an English `text`.

## Script steps

A script (CLI `r3d run`) is a JSON array of steps. A step is a command, a query, or one of:

- `{"type": "history.undo"}`: undo the last step.
- `{"type": "history.redo"}`: redo the last undone step.
- `{"type": "batch", "commands": [...]}`: run commands atomically as one undo step; if one fails, none is applied.

A string such as `"$3.created[0]"` refers to the result of an earlier step (step 3, 0-based, then the path `.created[0]`; `[n]` indexes arrays, `.name` reads fields). It must be the whole string; `$$` writes a literal `$`. References keep scripts independent of ID allocation.

## Commands

Document edits. Every command can be undone.

### `avatar.set`

Set the avatar's body: masculinity (0 feminine – 1 masculine) and height, bust, waist and hips in cm. The 3D body is fitted to these measurements; avatar.get reports what it actually measures.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "Body": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "Body measurements (cm), the input of the avatar fitting.",
      "properties": {
        "bust_cm": {
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "height_cm": {
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "hips_cm": {
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "masculinity": {
          "description": "0 = feminine body, 1 = masculine body.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "waist_cm": {
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "masculinity",
        "height_cm",
        "bust_cm",
        "waist_cm",
        "hips_cm"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Set the avatar's measurements.",
  "properties": {
    "body": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Body",
      "description": "Measurements in cm; `masculinity` 0 = feminine body, 1 = masculine."
    },
    "preset": {
      "description": "Name of the preset the measurements come from, if any.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "body"
  ],
  "title": "AvatarSet",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.create_rect`

Create a rectangular panel. Returns the panel, then its 4 points (counter-clockwise from the origin), then its 4 edges.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Create a rectangular panel.",
  "properties": {
    "grain_angle_deg": {
      "default": 90.0,
      "description": "Grainline angle in degrees from +X. Defaults to 90 (vertical).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "height": {
      "description": "Height in mm (> 0).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "Panel name. Defaults to \"Panel N\".",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "origin": {
      "default": [
        0.0,
        0.0
      ],
      "description": "Bottom-left corner on the board, in mm. Defaults to `[0, 0]`.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": "array"
    },
    "width": {
      "description": "Width in mm (> 0).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "width",
    "height"
  ],
  "title": "PanelCreateRect",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.mirror`

Create a linked mirror copy of a panel (e.g. left/right pieces). The copy follows every later change of its source; move it with panel.translate, or make it independent with panel.unlink. Returns the copy, then its points, then its edges.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Create a linked mirror copy of a panel.",
  "properties": {
    "axis_dir": {
      "description": "Direction of the mirror axis. Defaults to vertical `[0, 1]`.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "axis_origin": {
      "description": "A point on the mirror axis (mm). Defaults to a vertical axis placed\nso the copy sits to the right of the source with a 50 mm gap.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "Name of the copy. Defaults to \"<source name> (mirror)\".",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "panel": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "panel"
  ],
  "title": "PanelMirror",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.place`

Place a panel around the body for the 3D simulation: angle (0 front, 90 left side, 180 back, 270 right side), height of its top in cm, distance from the body in mm. Unplaced panels are not simulated.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Place a panel around the body for the simulation.",
  "properties": {
    "angle_deg": {
      "description": "Angle around the body (degrees): 0 front, 90 the body's left side,\n180 back, 270 right side.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "offset_mm": {
      "default": 30.0,
      "description": "Distance from the body at the start of the simulation (mm,\ndefault 30).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "panel": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
    },
    "top_cm": {
      "description": "Height of the panel's top above the floor (cm).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "panel",
    "angle_deg",
    "top_cm"
  ],
  "title": "PanelPlace",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.delete`

Delete a panel with its points, edges, notches and internal lines. Linked mirror copies of it become independent. Destructive: requires "confirm": true.

**Destructive**: requires `"confirm": true`.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Delete a panel with everything attached to it.",
  "properties": {
    "confirm": {
      "default": false,
      "description": "Must be `true`: deleting is destructive (still undoable).",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "panel": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "panel"
  ],
  "title": "PanelDelete",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `point.move`

Move a contour point to a new position in mm. Curve handles attached to the point move with it. The panel may end up self-intersecting; `panel.get` reports it.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PointId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a point, e.g. `point:1`.",
      "pattern": "^point:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Move a contour point.",
  "properties": {
    "point": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PointId"
    },
    "to": {
      "description": "New position in mm.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "point",
    "to"
  ],
  "title": "PointMove",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

```json
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
```

### `edge.set_curve`

Make an edge a straight line or a cubic Bézier curve (absolute control points in mm).

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "CurveSpec": {
      "description": "Shape to give an edge.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "Straight segment.",
          "properties": {
            "kind": {
              "const": "line",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "Cubic Bézier; control points in absolute board coordinates (mm).",
          "properties": {
            "c1": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            },
            "c2": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            },
            "kind": {
              "const": "cubic",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "c1",
            "c2"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      ]
    },
    "EdgeId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a edge, e.g. `edge:1`.",
      "pattern": "^edge:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Turn an edge into a straight line or a cubic curve.",
  "properties": {
    "curve": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/CurveSpec"
    },
    "edge": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "edge",
    "curve"
  ],
  "title": "EdgeSetCurve",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `internal_line.add`

Draw an internal line (an open path of straight and cubic segments, in mm) on a panel, e.g. a fold or placement line. Returns the line.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "SegmentSpec": {
      "description": "One segment of an internal line, starting where the previous one ended.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "properties": {
            "kind": {
              "const": "line",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "to": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "to"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "properties": {
            "c1": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            },
            "c2": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            },
            "kind": {
              "const": "cubic",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "to": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "c1",
            "c2",
            "to"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Draw an open path inside a panel.",
  "properties": {
    "panel": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
    },
    "segments": {
      "description": "At least one segment.",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/SegmentSpec"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "start": {
      "description": "Start point (mm).",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "panel",
    "start",
    "segments"
  ],
  "title": "InternalLineAdd",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `seam.add`

Sew two whole edges together. Points are matched along the edges, start to start unless a side is reversed (use seam.flip if the seam looks twisted). An edge can be in one seam only. Returns the seam.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "EdgeId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a edge, e.g. `edge:1`.",
      "pattern": "^edge:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "SeamSideSpec": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "One side of a new seam.",
      "properties": {
        "edge": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
        },
        "reversed": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Walk this edge from its end point instead of its start.",
          "type": "boolean"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "edge"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Sew two edges together.",
  "properties": {
    "a": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/SeamSideSpec"
    },
    "b": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/SeamSideSpec"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "a",
    "b"
  ],
  "title": "SeamAdd",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `seam.remove`

Remove a seam (the edges are no longer sewn).

```json
  "title": "SeamRemove",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "SeamId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a seam, e.g. `seam:1`.",

    }
  },
```

### `edge.lengthen`

Lengthen (mm > 0) or shorten (mm < 0) the garment at an open edge such as a hem: the edge moves along its panel's grain, and so do the edges it continues into across seams (the whole hemline), so sewn sides stay matched. Linked mirror copies follow their source.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "EdgeId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a edge, e.g. `edge:1`.",
      "pattern": "^edge:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Move an open edge, and the line it continues across seams, along the\ngrain.",
  "properties": {
    "edge": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId",
      "description": "An open (unsewn) edge: a hem, a sleeve end, a neckline."
    },
    "mm": {
      "description": "How far to move it (mm): positive makes the garment longer.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "edge",
    "mm"
  ],
  "title": "EdgeLengthen",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `pin.add`

Pin the cloth: the panel's cloth within 3 cm of `at` (pattern mm) is held still at `position` (3D metres) during the simulation. Returns the pin.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Pin the cloth in 3D.",
  "properties": {
    "at": {
      "description": "The pinned point on the pattern, `[x, y]` in mm.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": "array"
    },
    "panel": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
    },
    "position": {
      "description": "Where it is held in 3D, `[x, y, z]` in metres (Y up, the avatar's\nfeet at y = 0).",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 3,
      "minItems": 3,
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "panel",
    "at",
    "position"
  ],
  "title": "PinAdd",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `pin.remove`

```json
}
```

</details>

## Actions

Operations that write files (not undoable). Paths are relative to the project folder and cannot leave it.

### `export.svg`

Export all panels as an SVG at 1:1 scale (cutting and sewing lines, notches, internal lines, grainlines, labels, 100 mm test square). Returns the written path, relative to the project folder.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Export the pattern as SVG at 1:1 scale.",
  "properties": {
    "path": {
      "description": "Output path relative to the project folder. Defaults to\n`exports/<project name>.svg`.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "ExportSvg",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `simulate`

Drape the placed and sewn panels on the avatar for a number of frames (1/60 s each, deterministic) and cache the result in the project, so `r3d render --view 3d` shows it. Returns the garment's extent, how open the seams are and whether the cloth has settled.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Drape the garment headless and cache the result.",
  "properties": {
    "frames": {
      "default": 300,
      "description": "Frames of 1/60 s to simulate (1–3600, default 300 = 5 s).",
      "format": "uint32",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "title": "Simulate",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `export.pdf`

Export all panels as a PDF at 1:1 scale, tiled on A4/Letter pages (labelled A1, A2…, with overlap guides) or on one large page. Print at 100 % and check the 100 mm test square. Returns the written path and page count.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PaperSpec": {
      "description": "Page layout of a PDF export.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "a4",
          "description": "A4 tiles to print at home.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "letter",
          "description": "US Letter tiles to print at home.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "single",
          "description": "One page as large as the pattern (plotter, print shop).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Export the pattern as a PDF at 1:1 scale.",
  "properties": {
    "paper": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PaperSpec",
      "default": "a4",
      "description": "`a4` (default) or `letter` tiles with overlap and assembly guides,\nor `single` for one large page."
    },
    "path": {
      "description": "Output path relative to the project folder. Defaults to\n`exports/<project name>.pdf`.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "ExportPdf",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>
